titleText.en: For years, I took the wrong lesson from that Monster Cable experiment and only listened to my music through alligator-clipped coat hangers.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive supplies an empty title-text attribute, preserved exactly in the Spanish field; the English field preserves the complete official title text. The Spanish raster localizes the dialogue and sale signs, preserves technical labels as audited exclusions, joins the visible AL-/TAVOCES, ALTA-/VOCES, SABO-/REAR, and SIS-/TEMA line wraps as single words, and prints CLIC as a lexical sound effect.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cable can name an electrical or signal-carrying wire, not only a television service.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to (links one connector type to another)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In descriptions of adapters and cables, a links the connector at one end to the connector at the other end.

example.es: Compré un adaptador de USB a HDMI.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: For connectors, hembra describes a socket that receives a plug. A repeated pair such as hembra-hembra says both ends are sockets.
Altavoces is the plural of altavoz, a device that produces sound.

example.es: Los altavoces están junto al televisor.
example.en: The speakers are next to the television.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cutre is informal and dismissive. It describes something as shabby, low-quality, or embarrassingly cheap.
Oír means to perceive a sound. Its written accent keeps the two vowel sounds in separate syllables.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: they shoot at; they fire at
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Disparan is a present form of disparar for they or you plural. A short object word can identify the target.

example.en: The guards fire into the air.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Saborear literally means to savor a flavor. It can also mean taking time to enjoy or appreciate an experience in detail.

example.en: I want to savor every moment.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Detalle names one small, specific part of a larger whole.
Bello is an evaluative adjective. It changes to bella for a feminine singular noun and to bellos or bellas in the plural.
Paisaje can describe the visible scenery of a place and also appears figuratively in compounds such as paisaje sonoro.

example.es: El paisaje cambia junto al mar.
example.en: The landscape changes by the sea.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sonoro describes something made of, relating to, or rich in sound.

example.es: El museo creó un mapa sonoro.
example.en: The museum created a sound map.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Musical has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns; add -es for the plural.
Jamás is a strong way to say “never.” Like nunca, it can appear after a verb already negated with no, or before the verb without no.
Escuchado is the completed-action form of escuchar. It follows a form of haber: he escuchado, has escuchado, and so on.

example.en: I have never heard that song.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ripeo is computing slang for a digital copy extracted from another recording or medium. Ripeos is plural.

example.es: Guardó varios ripeos de sus discos.
example.en: He saved several rips of his discs.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you say (in a dismissive or conceding response)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Digas is a special form of decir for one familiar listener. Fixed responses such as lo que tú digas use it to concede or dismiss whatever the other person says.
Vatio is the Spanish unit name for a watt, a measure of power. Vatios is plural.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins de sobra
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De combines with sobra to form de sobra, which says there is more than enough.

example.en: We have more than enough food.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: more than enough; surplus (in de sobra)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sobra normally relates to something left over. In de sobra, it completes a fixed expression for an ample surplus.
Broma is a humorous remark, trick, or prank; context distinguishes a spoken joke from an action played on someone.
An audiófilo is a person strongly interested in high-quality sound reproduction and audio equipment. This masculine or mixed-group plural keeps the written accent.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: are (as part of hacen falta, are needed)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In hacer falta, hacer changes to agree with what is needed. Hacen is used when the needed people or things are plural.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: needed; necessary (as part of hacer falta)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Falta combines with a form of hacer to say that someone or something is needed. It stays singular in this expression even when hacen is plural.
Cambiar can mean altering something or replacing one item with another; the surrounding object supplies the exact sense.

example.en: I am going to replace the battery.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bombilla is the common word in Spain for the replaceable electric bulb in a lamp.
Apreciar can mean valuing someone or recognizing and enjoying a quality in something.
Remate can be the final touch that completes something. In a joke, it is the line that delivers the payoff.

example.es: El remate del chiste sorprendió a todos.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Chiste is a joke told for humor, often with a setup and a final punchline.
A códec is software or a method that encodes and decodes digital audio or video, often compressing it to use less data.

example.es: Este códec reduce el tamaño del audio.
example.en: This codec reduces the audio size.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins ya que, because or since
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ya and que form a causal connector. This fixed ya does not mean “already.”

example.es: Me fui, ya que era tarde.
example.en: I left because it was late.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; completes ya que, because or since
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Que completes the fixed causal connector ya que and introduces the reason that follows.

example.es: Cerramos, ya que no había clientes.
example.en: We closed because there were no customers.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce a reason with a phrase meaning “because” or “since”?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use ya que before the reason.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ya que is a fixed two-word connector. It introduces an explanation treated as known or relevant; the verb after it uses the ordinary statement form when the reason is presented as a fact.

example.es: Tomamos el autobús, ya que llovía.
example.en: We took the bus because it was raining.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you refer to the complete collection of sounds in a place or experience?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Paisaje literally means landscape, and sonoro relates to sound. Together they form the established term “soundscape,” covering the sounds that characterize an environment or recording.

example.es: Grabaron el paisaje sonoro del bosque.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you concede or dismissively accept whatever another person says?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Lo que refers to “whatever” is said, tú names one familiar listener for emphasis, and digas is the special form used in this open-ended concession. Tone can make the response sincere or dismissive.

example.es: De acuerdo, lo que tú digas.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that there is more than enough of something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use de sobra after the thing or amount that is plentiful.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The two words form a fixed expression for an ample surplus. It can follow nouns such as tiempo or dinero, or a verb such as haber or tener.

example.en: We have more than enough space.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you refer to a set of equipment that reproduces audio?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De links sistema to sonido to name the system's function. The expression can cover speakers, an amplifier, and related audio equipment.

example.es: Instalaron un sistema de sonido nuevo.
example.en: They installed a new sound system.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something is needed?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of hacer followed by falta; hacer agrees with what is needed.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: For one needed thing, use hace falta. For several, use hacen falta. The needed item acts like the grammatical subject, so the form of hacer changes even though falta stays singular.

example.es: Hace falta una llave, pero hacen falta dos tornillos.
example.en: One key is needed, but two screws are needed.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the final comment undermine the criticism of the speakers?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The supposed audio expert demands high fidelity while relying on heavily compressed sources and an even lower-quality phone connection.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Audiophiles value accurate sound reproduction. The speaker mocks cheap equipment, yet listens to low-bitrate video rips; the call's still lower bitrate then becomes the excuse for withholding the punchline. The mismatch between claimed standards and actual listening conditions drives the joke.

example.es: Un audiófilo comparó dos grabaciones con distinta compresión.
example.en: An audiophile compared two recordings with different compression.
